claims.text: Compositional diversity in multicomponent HEAs produces local lattice distortions.
Combining enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics with machine-learning interatomic potentials can efficiently determine HEA melting and liquid thermodynamics.
Enhanced sampling enables efficient exploration of the free-energy landscape connecting solid and liquid HEA states.
Enhanced-sampling techniques overcome the high free-energy barriers associated with melting.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can accurately capture complex multicomponent interactions in HEAs.
The combined approach enables precise calculation of solid–liquid free-energy differences.
Solid–liquid free-energy calculations can be used to determine melting temperature.
The approach can determine enthalpy and entropy of fusion.
The approach can determine the volume change at melting.
The approach can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
Predicted melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting volume change will agree with high-resolution experiments to within 10%.
The less-than-10% performance will hold across diverse HEA compositions.
Traditional calorimetry, CALPHAD, or standard atomistic simulation is either low-resolution or computationally prohibitive for broad HEA compositional exploration.
The vast compositional space of HEAs creates a need for efficient computational exploration tools.
The proposed method is applicable only within composition ranges for which its ML potentials have reliable training data and validation.
Performance may be limited at extreme compositional limits.
Metastable phases or phase separation may complicate the HEA free-energy landscape and limit performance.
The quantitative error margins and universal transferability of ML potentials across HEA compositions have not yet been established by systematic experiment.
Consistent deviations greater than 10% for all four fusion parameters across multiple HEAs would falsify the proposed approach.
